title: Option-byte self-enforcement delta: pin WRP1A/OEM-lock masks on silicon, write OEM keys to 0xFFFFFFFF in Phase A, measure the WHOLE slot window (declared length + 0xFF tail) in FSBL and secure world, and escalate a persistent tz-1 mismatch or an OBLRSTF boot to wipe instead of halt
threat: Transit attacker at RDP-0 plants an OEM1/OEM2 regression password (write-only, invisible to the SWD dump) so the later RDP-2 is reversible; parks a payload in the unmeasured tail of a slot (FSBL hashes only manifest-declared secure_len/ns_len); or glitches/reloads option bytes at boot — today the tripwire halts with secrets intact and ignores WRP1A/OEM by design.
proposal: (1) Close #46/#270: pin OEM1LOCK/OEM2LOCK and WRP1A bit positions on a sacrificial RDP-0 board with a positive detection (provision an OEM1 key, confirm the predicate trips), flip OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED/WRP1A_MASK_PINNED; Phase A writes OEM1KEYR1/2 and OEM2KEYR1/2 = 0xFFFFFFFF before programming RDP=0xCC and asserts NSSR OEMxLOCK clear afterwards; (2) FSBL verify_images hashes [secure_base, SLOT_SECURE_CAPACITY) and [ns_base, SLOT_NS_CAPACITY) with the tail required to be 0xFF (or random-filled at first boot and pinned, Krux model), and measured_boot::firmware_hash covers the same windows; fw_update COMMIT verifies the tail is erased; (3) FSBL reads RCC_CSR before the secure world and refuses to branch on OBLRSTF/IWDG/WWDG (secure world already classifies these — reset_cause.rs — but only after the FSBL has already measured and branched); (4) tz-1 persistent mismatch and Phase-A profile mismatch after RDP-2 arm the page-125 wipe flag before halting (Trezor secret_safety_erase); pre-RDP-2 mismatch keeps the current halt-unlocked-returnable policy.
rationale: Trezor's boardloader treats any option-byte difference as an attack and wipes; it explicitly zeroes the write-only OEM keys because the lock bits are the only observable. pq1 already has the predicates but they are unpinned and fail closed, so the production profile cannot pass; and the compressible-firmware assumption Donjon used to bypass Trezor's hash check applies to pq1's unmeasured slot tails. All firmware, mostly small, and it hardens the one anchor invariant #10 rests on.
repo_evidence: shared/src/lockdown.rs:264-290 (OEM lock bits 26/27, OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED=false → oem_locks_absent fails closed), :513-514
secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:179-191 (Phase A reads oem_lock_status_raw but no OEM key write exists; grep 'OEM1KEYR' -> none)
fsbl/src/optbytes.rs:24-30 ('deliberately does NOT act on WRP1A or the OEM locks'; halt only)
fsbl/src/verify.rs:40-65 (hash_flash_region(secure_base, secure_len) / (ns_base, ns_len) — manifest lengths, tail unmeasured)
secure/src/reset_cause.rs:1-38, :170 (OBLRSTF classified in secure world only; fsbl/src has no RCC_CSR flag read)
secure/src/fw_update/staging.rs:44-90 (0xFF padding within declared length; no tail check at COMMIT)
vendor_precedent: Trezor option_bytes.c:210-222 (OEM keys 0xFFFFFFFF) + :247-250 (OEM lock check) + boardloader main.c:325-340 (mismatch → secret_safety_erase); reset_flags.c (written, uncalled); Krux TC Flash Hash fills empty flash and hashes the whole region.
risks: Wipe-on-mismatch after RDP-2 is a brick lever for an FI attacker who can fake a mismatch — require a persistent two-pass mismatch (the existing F-2 sentinel pattern) and keep it off bench builds. OEM key write requires the silicon-pin evidence first; done blind it could itself set a lock. Whole-slot hashing adds ~2x FSBL verify time on pq1 (2.9 s measured today) — stays under the 4 s window only if the HASH peripheral is used in the FSBL. OBLRSTF is also set by a legitimate first-boot RDP-2 launch, so the FSBL rule must whitelist the journaled Phase-A path.
